title: SAFETY FOR THE ONE WHO ACTED UNINTENTIONALLY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'These six towns you give will be your cities of refuge. Give three on this side of the Jordan and three in Canaan as cities of refuge. These six towns will be a place of refuge for Israelites and for foreigners residing among them, so that anyone who has killed another accidentally can flee there.'" - Num 35:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The cities of refuge were placed strategically — three on each side of the Jordan — so that no one would be too far from safety. And notice who was included: not only Israelites, but "foreigners residing among them." The protection of these cities extended to everyone living in the land, including outsiders. God's provision of refuge was not reserved for a privileged few but open to all who needed it.

This detail is precious. God's mercy reaches beyond the boundaries we might expect. The foreigner, the outsider, the one who did not belong by birth — they too could flee to the city and find safety. God's care did not stop at ethnic lines. His refuge was available to any who came in need.

This foreshadows the wide-open welcome of the gospel. In Christ, the refuge God provides is not for one nation only but for all peoples. Jesus came to be a Saviour for the whole world — for Jew and Gentile, near and far, insider and outsider alike. Paul rejoices that in Christ there is no longer any dividing wall, and that those who were once far off have been brought near (Eph 2:13-14).

No one who flees to Christ is turned away because of their background, their past, or their status. The refuge is open to all. Whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved (Rom 10:13). If you have ever felt like an outsider, unsure whether God's mercy could be for you, hear this good news: the City of Refuge welcomes everyone who comes. Run to Jesus. There is room, and there is safety, for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever wondered whether God's mercy is truly for someone like you?
2. How does the inclusion of foreigners in these cities reflect the gospel's wide welcome?
3. Who around you needs to hear that Christ's refuge is open to them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Merciful God, thank You that Your refuge in Christ is open to all who come, with no one turned away. Assure me of my welcome in Jesus, and help me to point others to the safety found in Him. Amen.
